metaDescription: TV stands under $300 compared on width, TV size rating, depth, power outlets and storage, with honest notes on engineered wood, fluting and cable holes.
expertTake: The Bifins 62.2 inch fluted stand is the best overall pick because it lists exact dimensions, a 150 pound top rating and cable management. The AMERLIFE 66 inch is the best value for a farmhouse look with a stated TV size. Skip very wide stands in a small room, because a 95 inch console dominates a wall that a 60 inch unit would leave breathing space.
introParagraphs: A TV stand does four jobs: it holds the screen at a comfortable height, hides the boxes and cables, adds storage and sets the tone of the room. At the upper end of a modest budget, the useful differences are width against TV size, depth for the TV's feet, and whether the stand has power and cable management built in.

The cap reflects listing prices on the day we updated the guide, and prices move often. We kept the lineup distinct from our lower cap TV stand guides and focused on stands with a stated TV size or rating. We have not handled any of these stands, so our judgments rest on specifications and patterns in owner feedback, including how engineered wood and sliding doors age.

products.name: Bifins 62.2 Inch Walnut Fluted TV Stand, 15.75 x 29.5 in, 150 lb top, 4 doors
products.description:
This stand states its dimensions, 62.2 inches wide, 15.75 deep and 29.5 high, and a top rating of 150 pounds, along with a stated TV size of up to 70 inches. The walnut finish has fluted panels and arched contours, four push-to-open doors hide boxes and cables, and a cable management system keeps the back tidy. It reads as a mid-century piece that costs far less than the style suggests.

The tradeoff is that push-to-open doors rely on latches that can weaken, and a 15.75 inch depth is tight for some soundbars and consoles. Compared with the XIASLO, it is shorter and taller, with doors across the front, and it hides more. The fluting looks good but collects dust.

Measure your TV's feet and width before you order, since a 70 inch TV is wider than a 62 inch top. Tighten the cam locks after the first month. Wipe the fluting with a soft brush every few weeks.

cons: 15.75 inch depth is tight for some soundbars

products.name: AMERLIFE 66 Inch Farmhouse TV Stand, 66 x 15.6 x 28 in, barn door, up to 75 inch TV

specList.label: Dimensions
specList.value: 66 W x 15.6 D x 28 H in

products.description:
This stand lists 66 inches wide, 15.6 deep and 28 high and says it fits TVs up to 75 inches, with an X-pattern sliding barn door, metal hardware and a rustic finish. Adjustable shelves let you fit a soundbar, a game console or a streaming box. The farmhouse look suits a cottage or a casual family room.

The compromise is that sliding doors rely on a track, and a cheap track can jam or rattle after a year. Compared with the Bifins, the AMERLIFE is wider and more rustic, but it states no top rating in the compact data. A 15.6 inch depth is fine for most TVs but tight for a deep console.

Check that the doors slide freely at assembly and tighten the hardware. Place a coaster under a plant on top. Dust the X pattern with a brush.

products.name: XIASLO 70 Inch Fluted TV Stand for TVs up to 80 inch, dark walnut oak, drawer
products.description:
This is a 70 inch stand for TVs up to 80 inches, with a vertical fluted texture, a low profile, a storage drawer, two hidden cabinet doors and an open shelf. The dark walnut oak finish suits a modern room, and the low silhouette keeps a big screen from towering over the room. A drawer is handy for remotes and cables.

The tradeoff is that the compact data gives no depth or height, so check them against your TV's feet. Compared with the Bifins, the XIASLO is wider and lower, which suits an 80 inch TV but takes more wall. Low stands put the screen low, which suits a low sofa and not a high one.

Measure the wall and the TV's footprint before you order, because an 80 inch TV is wider than most stands. Keep the open shelf tidy with a basket. Tighten the fasteners after a month.

products.name: MXV 58 Inch Mid-Century TV Stand with Sliding Doors, 2 AC outlets, USB and Type-C
products.description:
This 58 inch stand has a built-in power strip with one USB port, one Type-C port and two AC sockets, so the TV, soundbar and game console can plug in at the stand and share one cord to the wall. Walnut sliding doors run on a track the listing calls smooth and quiet, and the fluted mid-century design matches the Bifins. The integrated power cuts the cable clutter behind the stand.

The tradeoff is that a built-in strip is not a surge protector unless the listing says so, and the compact data does not. Compared with the Bifins, the MXV is shorter and has power, but states no rating. Plug a surge protector into the wall and the stand's strip into that.

Do not overload the outlets with heaters or large appliances. Route the cord neatly through the back panel. Check the sliding doors after a month.

products.name: SUPERJARE Boho Rattan TV Stand for 65 inch TV, 53.9 x 13.7 in top, 2 cabinets
products.description:
This is a boho stand with rattan-decorated doors in two cabinets and a middle open shelf that adjusts for a streaming box or a console. The top measures 53.9 by 13.7 inches and the stand is described as suitable for TVs up to 55, 60 and 65 inches. Rattan doors give a natural texture that pairs with plants and woven baskets.

The compromise is the shallow 13.7 inch top, which limits TVs with wide feet, and the small cabinets, which hold less than a full-width unit. Compared with the Bifins, it has a lighter, airier look but less storage. Rattan can fray or crack if hit.

Check your TV feet against the 13.7 inch depth. Use a dust cloth on the rattan weave. Keep the cabinets from overloading, since they are narrow.

products.name: DHH 95.2 Inch Fluted TV Stand with Power, TVs up to 100 inch, drawer, 8 storage spaces
products.description:
This is the widest stand in the group at 95.2 inches, rated for TVs up to 100 inches, with two USB ports, two AC outlets and eight storage spaces including a drawer and hidden shelves. The mid-century fluted design and sliding door give it a furniture look. It is the one to choose for a very large TV on a long wall.

The tradeoff is size: a 95 inch stand needs a very long wall and often two people to lift. Compared with the Bifins, it has far more storage and power, but takes far more room. Long engineered wood spans can bow under the weight of a heavy TV, so check the supports.

Place it on a level floor and use the leveling feet. Do not overload the shelves. Check the screws after a month, since a long stand relies on them.

buyingCriteria.explanation: At this cap you can buy a stated TV size, built-in power, concealed storage or very large widths. The Bifins states a 150 pound top, the MXV and DHH add outlets, and the XIASLO and DHH fit 80 to 100 inch TVs. The cheaper stands in our lower cap guides skip these. Take the TV's foot-to-foot width from its spec sheet and compare it with the stand's usable top, since the TV's feet may sit wider than the screen's centre section.

The stand should be at least as wide as the TV's feet, and a stand a few inches wider than the TV looks balanced. A 65 inch TV is about 57 inches wide, so a 58 inch stand is the minimum and a 62 inch stand is comfortable. An 80 inch TV is about 70 inches wide. Allow at least 2 inches between the top of the stand and any shelf above, because a soundbar and a cable box need space to breathe.

Check the TV's foot spacing and depth, since a 13.7 inch top, like the SUPERJARE, can be too shallow for a TV with wide, deep feet. A soundbar needs room in front of the screen. Most stands at this cap are 15 to 16 inches deep. Check the weight of the TV from the spec sheet and compare it with the top rating, adding a 20 percent margin for a soundbar and a plant.

A stated top rating, such as the Bifins' 150 pounds, tells you the stand can hold a 65 to 75 inch TV, which weighs 50 to 100 pounds. Long engineered wood spans can bow, so look for a centre support. Check cam locks and screws. If the stand has glass doors or open shelves, remember that infrared remotes work through glass but not through solid doors.

Outlets and USB ports reduce cable clutter, but a stand's strip is not always surge protected. Plug the stand into a protected strip at the wall. Do not overload it with heaters. Choose a height that puts the middle of the screen near seated eye level, usually 40 to 44 inches from the floor to the centre of the screen.

Sliding doors need a good track, push-to-open doors need a good latch, and open shelves show clutter. Match the door type to your habits. Adjustable shelves help fit a soundbar or console. A stand that is 29 or 30 inches tall suits most sofas, while a very low stand may need a wall mount or a riser.

specDecoder.meaning: The largest TV the maker says the stand supports. It is a size guide and not always a weight guide. A stated TV size is a width guide and not a guarantee that the feet will fit.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Bifins lists up to 70 inches, AMERLIFE 75, XIASLO 80, SUPERJARE 65 and DHH 100.

specDecoder.meaning: The maximum weight the top can hold. It should exceed your TV weight with a margin. A 150 pound top rating is more than enough for most 70 inch TVs, but the stand also has to hold a soundbar and boxes.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Bifins lists 150 pounds, and the others do not state one.

specDecoder.meaning: The front to back measure of the top. It decides whether the TV's feet and soundbar fit. A depth under 15 inches can leave the TV's rear feet hanging over the edge.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Bifins is 15.75 inches, AMERLIFE 15.6 and SUPERJARE 13.7.

specDecoder.meaning: A vertical ridged texture on panels. It adds depth but collects dust. Fluting looks best in even light and can look busy in a room with strong patterns.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Bifins, XIASLO, MXV and DHH use fluting.

specDecoder.meaning: Sockets in the stand. Convenient, but check for surge protection. Power strips in furniture usually draw from a single cord, so total load matters.
specDecoder.watchFor: The MXV and DHH list outlets and USB ports.

howWeEvaluated.title: Dimensions and TV fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated each stand on the dimensions and TV size stated in its listing. The Bifins and AMERLIFE state full dimensions, and the XIASLO gives only width. We have not handled any of these stands.

howWeEvaluated.title: Rating and construction
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared top ratings and construction. The Bifins lists 150 pounds. Owner feedback patterns often mention bowing shelves and loose doors.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power and cables
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered outlets and cable management. The MXV and DHH include power, and the Bifins includes cable holes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Distinct from lower caps
howWeEvaluated.description: We avoided repeating our lower cap TV stand lineups and left out tabletop stands and risers. We do not publish ratings or review counts.

howWeEvaluated.title: Honest limits
howWeEvaluated.description: At this cap, stands are engineered wood. Listings often omit depth and rating, and we say so.
